title: Linkability of Student Submission Data
description: The student's submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) could be linked to their identity across different systems or time periods, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of their academic activities.

title: Identifiability of Student from Submission Data
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission timestamp creates a unique identifier that could reveal the student's identity even if other data is anonymized.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Assignment and Personal Data
description: The assignment work file and personal information could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Submission Data
description: The submission data could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission or storage, compromising the authenticity and accuracy of the assignment.

title: Student Identity Usurpation for Assignment Submission
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the student to submit assignments on their behalf, compromising the authenticity of the submission and potentially enabling academic dishonesty.

title: Unauthorized Access to Data in Transit
description: Student IDs, course information, file references, and role data transmitted from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service could be intercepted during transmission if not properly encrypted, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive academic information.

title: Linkability Across Systems
description: The transmitted data (student ID, course, file reference) could be linked with other datasets held by the institution or third parties, potentially creating comprehensive profiles of students and their academic activities.

title: Identification of Individuals
description: Student IDs included in the data flow could be used to identify specific individuals, potentially exposing personal academic information to unauthorized parties.

title: User Impersonation
description: If authentication mechanisms are weak, an attacker could impersonate a student or instructor to submit or access grading information, leading to unauthorized actions and potential academic fraud.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: An attacker could gain unauthorized access to the Assignment Store and retrieve student assignment files, student IDs, course information, and submission times without proper authentication or authorization controls.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Assignment Data
description: An attacker could modify assignment files, student IDs, course information, or submission times in the Assignment Store, potentially altering grades, falsifying submissions, or tampering with academic records.

title: Student Identification from Stored Data
description: The stored assignment data contains student IDs and course information that could be used to identify specific students, potentially leading to privacy violations if accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Linkability of Assignment Data to Other Records
description: Student assignment data could be linked with other student records (e.g., enrollment data, grades, personal information) to create comprehensive profiles of students, potentially enabling tracking across multiple systems.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Storing student assignment data with personal identifiers may violate privacy regulations such as FERPA, GDPR, or other educational data protection laws if proper consent, access controls, and data retention policies are not implemented.

title: Teacher Account Impersonation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a teacher by compromising their credentials, gaining unauthorized access to submission queues and potentially viewing or manipulating student work.
assumptions: Teacher authentication is not sufficiently secure; credentials could be stolen or guessed.

title: Unauthorized Student Data Disclosure
description: Student submission data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly enforced, potentially revealing student identities, grades, or work to individuals without legitimate access.
assumptions: Access control mechanisms may have vulnerabilities; teacher permissions may be overly broad.

title: Teacher-Student Relationship Linkability
description: The system could link a teacher's identity to specific student submissions they review, potentially creating privacy concerns about the relationship between educators and student data access patterns.
assumptions: Access logs or metadata could be used to trace which teacher reviewed which submissions.

title: Teacher Identification Through Access Patterns
description: A teacher could be identified through their unique access patterns to specific courses, submission queues, or time-based access, potentially revealing their teaching assignments or workload.
assumptions: Access logs are not anonymized; access patterns are unique enough to identify individuals.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Submission Queue
description: The Grades Portal Web App may collect more student data than necessary for the teacher's review task, including metadata that could reveal student identities or additional personal information.
assumptions: System collects full student profiles rather than minimal necessary information for grade review.

title: Student Identification via Submission Data
description: Student names and work content displayed to teachers can identify individual students, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties if teacher access is compromised or if data is logged.
assumptions: Teacher access controls are properly implemented; data is not unnecessarily retained beyond teaching purposes.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Work
description: Student work content and submission times may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the portal system has vulnerabilities, if teacher credentials are compromised, or if data is improperly logged/stored.
assumptions: Portal has adequate security controls; teacher access is properly authenticated and authorized.

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Sources
description: Student names, work content, and submission times can be linked with other data sources (e.g., enrollment records, assessment data), potentially creating comprehensive profiles of students beyond the intended educational purpose.
assumptions: Data is not integrated with external systems without proper consent; data minimization principles are followed.

title: Non-compliance with Educational Data Regulations
description: Sharing student names and work content may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent, data minimization, or retention policies are not followed.
assumptions: Institution has appropriate data governance policies; data sharing complies with applicable regulations.

title: Student and Grader Identification via IDs
description: The data flow includes student ID and grader ID fields that could be used to identify specific students and teachers, potentially exposing their identities to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: IDs are not properly anonymized or masked before storage/transmission

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grades and Feedback
description: Grades and written feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized individuals or systems if access controls are not properly implemented, potentially revealing sensitive academic performance information.
assumptions: Access controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized viewing of grade data

title: Linkability of Student Performance Data
description: The combination of student ID, grader ID, grade, and feedback text could be linked across multiple records to create detailed profiles of student performance and teaching patterns.
assumptions: Multiple data points can be correlated to identify patterns

title: Insecure Data Transmission of Sensitive Information
description: The data flow from teacher to grades portal may transmit sensitive grade and feedback information over unencrypted channels, exposing it to interception.
assumptions: Data transmission may not use proper encryption protocols

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grade Recording
description: Teachers may be able to deny having recorded specific grades or feedback if the system does not maintain proper audit trails or digital signatures.
assumptions: System may not implement adequate logging or authentication mechanisms

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records containing student IDs, grades, and feedback could be accessed by unauthorized individuals through database breaches, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Database lacks proper access controls or authentication mechanisms

title: Student Identification from Grade Data
description: Grade records with student IDs and course information could be used to identify specific students, potentially revealing their academic performance and creating privacy risks.
assumptions: Student IDs are not properly anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Linkability of Student Academic Records
description: Student IDs in grade records could be linked to other student data (e.g., enrollment records, personal information), creating comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple systems

title: Excessive Data Collection in Feedback Field
description: The feedback field may contain unnecessary personal information or sensitive comments that exceed what is needed for grading purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Feedback field is not properly scoped or validated

title: Lack of Grading Action Non-Repudiation
description: Grading actions may not be properly logged or audited, allowing graders to deny their grading decisions or modifications to grade records.
assumptions: Insufficient audit logging or timestamp validation

title: Grader Identity Usurpation
description: Unauthorized individuals could potentially impersonate graders or modify grade records by exploiting weak authentication or authorization mechanisms.
assumptions: Authentication system has vulnerabilities or weak access controls

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities in the system

title: Identity Usurpation for Grade Access
description: An attacker could impersonate a student to access their grades and feedback through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks.
assumptions: Assumes authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential compromise

title: Grade Data Integrity Compromise
description: Student grades and feedback could be tampered with, modified, or deleted by unauthorized actors, leading to inaccurate academic records.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient integrity controls or audit logging

title: Linkability of Grades to Student Identity
description: Grades could be linked to student identity in ways that create privacy risks, such as through cross-referencing with other data sources or metadata.
assumptions: Assumes grades are stored with identifiable metadata

title: Student Identification from Grade Data
description: Student identity could be inferred or directly identified from their grades and feedback data, potentially through unique grade patterns or feedback content.
assumptions: Assumes grade patterns or feedback may be distinctive enough for identification

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured.
assumptions: The portal lacks adequate encryption or access controls for the data transmission.

title: Student Identification from Grade Data
description: If grades and feedback are displayed with identifying information (e.g., student name, ID), an observer could identify the student from this data flow.
assumptions: The portal displays grades with student identifiers.

title: Grade Data Manipulation
description: An attacker could potentially alter the grades or teacher feedback during transmission if the data flow is not authenticated or integrity-protected.
assumptions: The system lacks proper authentication and integrity checks for the data flow.

title: Linkability of Academic Records
description: The student's grades and feedback could be linked to other data about the student (e.g., personal information, other courses), creating a comprehensive profile.
assumptions: The student's data is stored in systems that can be cross-referenced.

title: Student Account Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate the student to access their grades and feedback if authentication mechanisms are weak.
assumptions: The portal uses weak or compromised authentication.

title: Unauthorized Account Access
description: Parent's account credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized parties to access the parent's account and request grades for their child.
assumptions: Parent uses weak password or credentials are intercepted during transmission

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Grades
description: Child's grades could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through insecure data transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over unencrypted channels or access controls are insufficient

title: Child Identifiability from Grades Data
description: Grades data could be used to identify the specific child, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's academic performance and personal details.
assumptions: Grades are associated with identifiable information or can be cross-referenced with other data sources

title: Insecure Data Storage of Grades
description: Child's grades stored in the Grades Portal Web App could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems due to inadequate security measures.
assumptions: Data storage lacks proper encryption or access controls

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Academic Records
description: Child's grades, feedback, and submission history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Inadequate authentication/authorization mechanisms or network vulnerabilities exist

title: Linkability of Academic Data with Other Personal Information
description: The child's academic data could be linked with other personal information (e.g., identity, location, behavioral data) creating a comprehensive profile of the child.
assumptions: Data is shared across multiple systems or platforms

title: Unauthorized Access to Grades Portal by Non-Parent Users
description: Unauthorized individuals could access the portal and view the child's grades, feedback, and submission history through credential theft, session hijacking, or weak authentication.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not sufficiently robust

title: Inappropriate Identification of Child Through Academic Data
description: The parent could potentially identify or be identified through the child's academic data, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's educational status or performance.
assumptions: Data is used in contexts where identification is not intended
uncertainty_note: Less certain as parent is the intended recipient, but data could be misused

title: Deceptive Presentation of Academic Feedback
description: The parent could receive misleading or incomplete information about the child's grades, feedback, or submission history, potentially leading to incorrect conclusions about the child's academic performance.
assumptions: Data manipulation or incomplete data transmission occurs
uncertainty_note: Lower likelihood as this is a standard educational portal, but data integrity cannot be fully guaranteed

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Personal Data
description: School Administrator (EE4) has access to create, modify, and disable accounts and parent-child links containing names, emails, roles, and relationships. If access controls are insufficient or credentials are compromised, sensitive personal data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator has legitimate access but system lacks adequate access controls or authentication mechanisms

title: Malicious Data Manipulation by Administrator
description: School Administrator (EE4) can modify account information and parent-child relationships. Malicious actors with administrator privileges could alter, delete, or falsify this sensitive data, leading to incorrect records and potential harm to students and parents.
assumptions: Administrator account is compromised or misused for malicious purposes

title: Administrator Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate the School Administrator (EE4) to gain unauthorized access to the Grades Portal Web App (P1), potentially leading to unauthorized account creation, modification, or deletion of sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft occurs

title: Identification of Individuals from Account Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes account data including names, emails, and parent-child relationships. This data could be used to identify specific individuals, potentially leading to privacy violations if accessed inappropriately.
assumptions: Personal identifiers are stored and processed in the system

title: Data Disclosure During Account Management Operations
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) may expose sensitive account and relationship data during normal operations (e.g., during account creation, modification, or viewing). Inadequate data handling could lead to unintended disclosure.
assumptions: Data is transmitted or displayed without adequate protection

title: Unauthorized Modification of Account Records
description: The Assignment & Grading Service writes account records to the Account Directory. An attacker could intercept or manipulate this write operation to alter account information, potentially compromising user data integrity and privacy.
assumptions: The write channel between P2 and DS3 is not adequately protected against tampering.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Parent-Child Relationship Links
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory. An attacker could modify these relationships to create false familial connections or break legitimate ones, potentially affecting access controls or privacy expectations.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is sensitive and requires protection from unauthorized modification.

title: Linkability of Account Records via Parent-Child Relationships
description: Parent-child relationship links written to the account directory could be used by an observer to link different account records together, potentially revealing family relationships and enabling inference attacks on individual privacy.
assumptions: The parent-child relationship data is accessible to external observers or can be correlated across records.

title: Identification via Account Records
description: Account records written to the directory contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Account records contain sufficient PII to enable identification.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Account Record Writes
description: When the grading service writes account records, there may be no adequate audit trail or cryptographic proof to prevent denial of actions, making it difficult to verify who made changes to account data.
assumptions: The system does not implement comprehensive logging or digital signatures for write operations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Student Data
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted to third-party cloud hosting provider, creating risk of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal and educational information to unauthorized parties within or outside the provider's organization.

title: Data Tampering During Transmission
description: Nightly database backup and replication data transmitted to cloud provider could be intercepted or modified in transit, compromising data integrity of grades, assignments, and account information.

title: Unauthorized Access by Cloud Provider Personnel
description: Cloud hosting provider employees or contractors may have unauthorized access to stored student data including grades, assignments, and account directory information.

title: Student Identification Through Account Directory
description: Account directory data transmitted to cloud provider contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individual students.

title: Linkability of Student Records Across Systems
description: Combination of grade records, assignments, and account directory data could be linked across different systems or time periods to create comprehensive profiles of students.

title: Lack of Data Anonymization
description: Full records are transmitted without anonymization or pseudonymization, making it possible to identify individuals from the data.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database contains sensitive personal information about students, parents, and teachers. Unauthorized access could lead to disclosure of private academic and personal information.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls on the grade records database

title: Student and Parent Identification
description: Grade records can be used to identify specific students and their parents, potentially leading to unwanted attention, doxxing, or privacy violations.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiable information that can be cross-referenced

title: Linkability of Educational Data
description: Grade records can be linked with other data sources (enrollment, attendance, behavioral records) to create comprehensive profiles of students, parents, and teachers.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated

title: Inappropriate Data Exposure in Views
description: Assignment & Grading Service may expose sensitive grade information in student, parent, or teacher views without proper access controls or data masking.
assumptions: Views may not properly restrict data based on user roles

title: Educational Privacy Compliance Violation
description: Handling of grade records may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding student data protection and parental consent requirements.
assumptions: Data handling practices may not fully comply with applicable privacy laws

title: Unauthorized View Access
description: Students or parents may access grade views intended for other students or parents, leading to information leakage about other individuals.
assumptions: Authentication or authorization mechanisms may be insufficient
